description: Reusable archetype fragments for Learn companion videos.

archetypes.name: spotlight
archetypes.summary: Centered payoff frame with one dominant subject.
archetypes.content_shape: One conclusion, object, statement, or metric that deserves the frame.
archetypes.best_for: Openings, closings, reveals, decisive takeaways, and a single high-value comparison result.
archetypes.avoid_when: The beat must explain several peers, ordered steps, dependencies, or status details.
archetypes.weighted_object: The one subject or statement the learner should remember.
archetypes.default_ground: content-wash; hero-swoosh only when the beat earns the scarce payoff field.
archetypes.example_beat: Reveal that one policy decision controls the enrollment outcome.

archetypes.name: catalog
archetypes.summary: List-surface with one lifted row and count callout.
archetypes.content_shape: A small set of peer items with one item selected, compared, or emphasized.
archetypes.best_for: Roles, options, policy types, app categories, inventory, and choose-one decisions.
archetypes.avoid_when: Order, containment, causality, or dependencies carry the meaning.
archetypes.weighted_object: The lifted row, selected item, or count that resolves the choice.
archetypes.example_beat: Compare assignment types and lift the one used for the scenario.
archetypes.legacy_source: Derived from MD-102 console and dashboard patterns
archetypes.notes: Use when the beat explains role or item selection.

archetypes.name: layer-stack
archetypes.summary: Nested planes around a core object.
archetypes.content_shape: Nested scopes, boundaries, inheritance, or protection arranged outside-in or inside-out.
archetypes.best_for: Containment, trust boundaries, layered security, inheritance, and management scope.
archetypes.avoid_when: The items are peers, the explanation is chronological, or connections matter more than nesting.
archetypes.weighted_object: The protected core or the boundary whose effect is being explained.
archetypes.example_beat: Show device, identity, and policy layers converging on the managed endpoint.
archetypes.notes: Use for containment, inheritance, or boundary framing.

archetypes.name: timeline
archetypes.summary: State-track with carrier and lane events.
archetypes.content_shape: An ordered sequence in which state, timing, or cause-and-effect changes along a path.
archetypes.best_for: Workflows, lifecycle stages, ordered gates, countdowns, rollouts, and before-to-after change.
archetypes.avoid_when: The items are unordered, simultaneous, nested, or primarily connected as a system.
archetypes.weighted_object: The carrier or current state that moves the learner through the sequence.
archetypes.default_ground: content-wash; section-field only for a true segment transition.
archetypes.example_beat: Trace a device from registration through compliance evaluation to access.
archetypes.notes: Use for ordered gates and sequence logic.

archetypes.name: console
archetypes.summary: Panel + rows for explicit status checks.
archetypes.content_shape: Operational details expressed as checks, statuses, request fields, approvals, or outcomes.
archetypes.best_for: Portal-like evidence, approval flows, troubleshooting checks, request detail, and pass-or-fail status.
archetypes.avoid_when: The beat is conceptual, relational, emotionally decisive, or better understood as a sequence.
archetypes.weighted_object: The status change, approval, failed check, or field that determines the outcome.
archetypes.example_beat: Show three readiness checks, then change the blocking row from pending to passed.
archetypes.notes: Use for request detail, checklist, and approvals.

archetypes.name: blueprint
archetypes.summary: Node graph with links and tagged chips.
archetypes.content_shape: Components whose relationships, dependencies, ownership, or data flow carry the meaning.
archetypes.best_for: Architecture, service relationships, dependency maps, responsibility boundaries, and data flow.
archetypes.avoid_when: A simple list, one payoff, nested containment, or a strict procedure explains the idea more clearly.
archetypes.weighted_object: The key node, link, or handoff that explains how the system works.
archetypes.example_beat: Connect Intune, Microsoft Entra ID, and the device around the compliance decision.
archetypes.notes: Use for architecture and dependency explanation.
